props.doc:
Build the property form for the selected node.

Every field comes from the command version's own input_schema - the same
object the worker validates the call against. Nothing here is hand-written
per command, which is why adding a connector adds working forms for all of
its commands without touching the UI.
props.name: renderInspector

props.doc:
The vendor modes available for a response node's `mode` field.

Defender offers Full and Selective isolation; SentinelOne offers none;
its quarantine action offers five. The picker offers the union across the
EDRs that are actually configured, and the coverage panel above says which
vendor honours which - because a mode one EDR ignores is a silent change in
behaviour for half the estate.
props.name: modeOptions

props.doc:
The per-vendor panel for a response node.

This exists because EDR response actions are not interchangeable. It states
the coverage, names each EDR that can perform the action and what it means by
it, and lists the ones that cannot with the reason. An engineer reads this
while drawing, not after an execution half-failed.
props.name: renderCoverage

props.doc:
Retries and timeout.

The retry count applies only to errors the command declared retryable. A 401
is never retried whatever is set here - retrying an auth failure is how an
automation platform locks out the service account it depends on, and that is
not a decision left to whoever draws the playbook.
props.name: renderReliability

props.doc:
The compensating step for a mutating action.

The platform never invents a rollback. Where the command registry knows the
undo - isolate has release, block has unblock - the editor offers to create
that node and wire it, which is how a declared compensation gets written by
the person who knows it is needed rather than by nobody.
props.name: renderCompensation
